intro: Measured on one machine (Windows 11, Intel 13900K, RTX 4090) against a retail Xbox Series 1.0.2.1 package. Every row below is an outcome the project produces, not a plan; the commands that produce them are in the Build section, and the failures behind each number are in docs/boot_frontier.md.

stages.evidence: the title's PE32+ image maps at its preferred base, imports resolve through shims, static TLS is redirected for 53,246 slot-0 reads, heap and file system come from the host
26,616 SPIR-V modules indexed from 26,503 carved game modules plus the pipeline library; the pipeline library and FSPX repair are wired into make_game, so a fresh build reproduces the index
device, queues, allocators, descriptor heaps, command lists and pipelines answer on an RTX 4090; the retail boot reaches 11,986 D3D12 calls with 0 pipeline failures and no stand-in pipelines
factory, file open, zlib decompression; BCPack and swizzled reads still refuse rather than guess
the title gets well past renderer setup and into its own render code; it now stops on a container element it built empty (see the frontier), not on a shim refusal
console frame-event calls are answered, but the title has not yet completed one frame

counts.what: D3D12 calls in a retail boot
Refused graphics pipeline creations (console slot 57, before the conversion)

counts.value: 6 (VS, PS, DS, HS, GS and one more)

frontier.summary: a read at 0x10 because a small container element is null: the title builds the container empty and reads its first element as an object pointer, and its own null check then reaches a compiler trap. The null traces back to a pipeline state the title never received: console device slot 57 is graphics PSO creation (measured from the call itself - IID_ID3D12PipelineState, a root signature and six native-code stage pairs), and forwarding it by slot number turned 10,242 of those calls into refused CreateLifetimeTracker calls.
